column10: Fundamentals of programming using Python. Variables, control flow, functions, lists, and basic object-oriented concepts. No prior experience required.
Logic, sets, relations, functions, graph theory, combinatorics, and proof techniques essential for computer science.
HTML, CSS, and introductory JavaScript. Building static and simple dynamic web pages. No prerequisites.
Arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, heaps, hash tables, and graphs. Algorithm complexity analysis. Object-oriented design in Java.
Digital logic, binary arithmetic, assembly language, memory hierarchy, and CPU architecture fundamentals.
Sorting, searching, dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, graph algorithms, NP-completeness. Formal proof of correctness and time complexity.
Relational model, SQL, normalization, transactions, indexing, and query optimization. Requires CS201 with a grade of C or better.
Processes, threads, scheduling, memory management, file systems, and concurrency. Programming projects in C.
Software development lifecycle, requirements engineering, design patterns, testing strategies, and version control. Accepts CS201 or CS301 as prerequisite.
Network protocols, OSI model, TCP/IP, routing, security fundamentals, and socket programming.
Supervised and unsupervised learning, neural networks, evaluation methods, and feature engineering. Requires any 2 of: CS301, CS310, MATH250.
First semester of a two-semester capstone. Project selection, team formation, requirements specification, system design, and prototype. CS491 must be taken concurrently.
Second semester of capstone. Full implementation, testing, deployment, and public presentation of the completed system. CS490 must be taken concurrently.
Vectors, matrices, eigenvalues, and probability theory for computer scientists. Cross-listed with MATH department.
